## 1. Blocking findings

### B-1 — AC-10 is not satisfied: the P1 boundary is structural against the wrong failure mode

**Defect.** `implementation/FEATURE_TECH_PLAN.md` §4 proposes three stacked controls and
claims "defeating all three simultaneously is what would be required to violate P1."
Against the failure mode P1 and §41.4 actually name — *the AI layer originating a number
it presents* — controls 1, 2 and 4 are inert, and control 3 is not decidable as written.
The stack is one control deep at the point of interest.

**Failure scenario (the ordinary one, not an exotic one).** The AI Orchestration process
makes two legitimate Tool Gateway calls and receives two legitimate `MetricResult`
envelopes: 1Y portfolio return `0.0840`, benchmark return `0.0610`. It then writes:
"you beat your benchmark by **2.3 percentage points**." That number was originated by
the language model. Trace it through the controls:

- **Control 1 (credential/network isolation)** — not engaged. No database was touched and
  no endpoint outside the Tool Gateway was called. The control's stated failure signature
  ("an authentication failure or connection refusal") never fires.
- **Control 2 (typed envelope requiring a state)** — not engaged. It constrains what the
  AI *receives*, not what it emits. It is a P5 control presented as a P1 control.
- **Control 4 (import lint)** — not engaged. No import occurred.
- **Control 3 (grounding-check middleware)** — the only live control. `2.3` resolves to no
  logged tool call, so it should block. Whether it does depends entirely on how
  "material" and "resolve to" were implemented, which the plan does not specify.

So AC-10's test — *"a reviewer must be able to describe how a violation would fail"* — I
can answer for "the AI queries the ledger directly" (crisply: connection refused) and I
**cannot** answer for "the AI does arithmetic on values it was legitimately given," which
is the violation P1 exists to prevent. AC-10 is **not satisfied**.

**Sub-finding B-1a: "material" is undecidable as specified, and its ambiguity resolves
in the unsafe direction.** Control 3 "scans the response for numeric tokens and requires
each material one to resolve to a specific, logged Tool Gateway call." Three concrete
cases the specification does not decide:

1. *Reformatting.* The tool returned `0.1300`; the response says "about 13%". No token
   match. Either the check false-positives, or the implementer adds numeric-equivalence
   normalization — at which point `2.3` in the scenario above may normalize into a match
   against `0.084`/`0.061` under a loose enough rule.
2. *Non-claims.* "9988.HK", "2026", "the top 3 holdings", "your 5-year window" are numeric
   tokens that are not claims. Excluding them *is* the definition of "material," and it is
   left to whoever writes the middleware.
3. *Cross-turn reference.* "Last month your HK exposure was 22%" cites a number fetched in
   an earlier request, so it is absent from *this* request's audit trail (§4.3 scopes the
   check to "the same request's audit trail"). It blocks correctly-grounded output.

Cases 1 and 3 generate false rejections, and the pressure from false rejections is always
to loosen the rule until the product works. A control whose strictness is set at
implementation time by whoever is trying to make the demo pass is a guideline wearing a
mechanism's clothes. Source PRD §22.3 does use the word "material," so the plan inherits
it honestly — but §22.3 states a *requirement*, and T4 is supposed to supply the
*mechanism*. The mechanism has to decide the word the requirement leaves open.

**Sub-finding B-1b: Control 1's "exactly one network destination" is contradicted by the
plan's own open item.** §4.1 states the AI process "can reach exactly one network
destination: the Tool Gateway's interface." §8.2 logs "AI model/provider for AI
Orchestration — which LLM provider/model powers CP9" as undecided. If CP9 uses a hosted
model, the AI Orchestration process must have egress to the provider, so the destination
count is two and the second is an external channel carrying untrusted response text.
The control as written is then not implementable as stated, and its failure signature no
longer distinguishes "AI reached for data it should not have" from "AI called its model."
The plan asserts the provider choice "has no bearing on the T4 structural boundary" — for
this control it does.

**Contract violated.** `specs/FEATURE_PRD.md` AC-10; source PRD P1, §22.3, NFR-002, §41.4;
CP9 exit criterion ("AI cannot produce a material portfolio number that is not available
through deterministic tools/structured facts").

**Why this is blocking at CP0 rather than CP9.** ADR-P4 proposes to pin this three-control
mechanism as a hard-to-reverse decision whose own stated cost of change is "re-auditing
every AI code path." The plan's §11 self-assessment records AC-10 as "Satisfied as
designed." If the HG1 package carries that forward, the owner approves a boundary against
the wrong failure mode and pays for it at CP9. Note that `reviews/gates/CP0_RECONCILIATION.md`
§1 also records the P1 row as "Coherent" — correctly, since the design does not depend on
a control the plan omits. Coherence between the two artifacts is not the same as
sufficiency of the control, and this finding is about the latter.

**Not a demand for a specific fix.** What the mechanism should be is `engineer`'s to
propose and HG1's to approve. What I can say is that AC-10's bar is not met until a
reviewer can describe the failure path for the derived-number case, and that "material"
needs a decidable definition before ADR-P4 is pinned.

### B-2 — The shipped `MetricResult` admits states the design contract cannot render, and PD-0006's claim that D3 needs no rework is false

**Defect.** `src/product_contract/metric_state.py` deliberately imposes no coupling
between `reason_code` and `sufficiency_state`. `designs/FEATURE_DESIGN.md` §D3.2 states
the opposite as its rendering rule:

> Each reason code … "Attaches as the explanatory clause on whichever sufficiency state it
> modifies (per D3.1, always `LIMITED` or `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` — **a reason code never
> modifies `AVAILABLE`**, since if there were a live blocking reason the metric could not
> be fully available)."

`PD-0006` (amended 2026-09-03) blesses `AVAILABLE` + `STALE_DATA` and simultaneously
states that "**D3** … was authored to exactly this reading and needs no rework." Those
cannot both be true. D3.2 has **no rendering** for an `AVAILABLE` metric carrying a reason
code, and `tests/product/test_metric_result.py::StaleDataNarrowingTests` pins exactly that
combination — with a value — as intended behaviour.

**Failure scenario 1 (the disclosed case, unrouted).** CP1 produces
`MetricResult(value=1.30, sufficiency_state=AVAILABLE, reason_code=STALE_DATA)`. CP7
renders it by D3.2, which is keyed on sufficiency state first and says a reason code never
modifies `AVAILABLE`. The reason code is dropped. The user sees an unqualified `1.30`.
The staleness disclosure that PD-0006 said would be carried by the D5 freshness axis is
not carried by `MetricResult` either (see the sizing in §2.3 below), so it is carried
nowhere. Violates P10 and §11.2.

**Failure scenario 2 (the wider blast radius, and the more serious one).** The narrowing
was argued for `STALE_DATA` and implemented as a blanket absence of coupling. So this is
also constructible and is accepted by the type:

```
MetricResult(value=1.30, sufficiency_state=AVAILABLE, reason_code=MISSING_BENCHMARK)
MetricResult(value=1.30, sufficiency_state=AVAILABLE, reason_code=CALCULATION_ERROR)
```

A CP4 beta computation whose benchmark series is missing sets `reason_code=MISSING_BENCHMARK`
and — because nothing forces the demotion — leaves `sufficiency_state=AVAILABLE` with a
value. The type accepts it, no test catches it, and D3.2 renders a bare `1.30`. That is a
judgment presented with no reference point (**P4**), a number the product cannot justify
(**§41.3 false precision**), and a metric state the UI cannot honor (**§32**: "UI and AI
must honor this state"). `AVAILABLE` + `CALCULATION_ERROR` + a value is indefensible under
any reading of §32.

**On whether the narrowing was correct — the question referred to this review.** The
premise was right and the scope was wrong.

- Right: `AVAILABLE` + `STALE_DATA` is a real case, PD-0006 establishes it, and forcing
  every stale metric to `LIMITED` would fire constantly and carry no information. Refusing
  to invent `quant_analyst`'s staleness threshold was correct and is squarely within
  `roles/engineer.json`'s limits.
- Wrong: the engineer's stated dilemma — option (b), that coupling would "require inventing
  which reason codes are exempt — also not this module's call" — is not true on the record.
  **PD-0006 already supplies the exemption list, verbatim:** *"`STALE_DATA` is not shaped
  like the other five reason codes. The other five describe a condition under which a
  metric cannot be properly computed."* The rule
  `reason_code ∈ {UNSUPPORTED_ASSET, MISSING_BENCHMARK, MISSING_COST_BASIS,
  MISSING_FX_HISTORY, CALCULATION_ERROR} ⇒ sufficiency_state ≠ AVAILABLE` requires no
  threshold, no `quant_analyst` input, and no freshness axis. It was available, and the
  narrowing went past it.

So: **the narrowing does leave a hole through which a metric can present a number it
should not.** Not through `STALE_DATA` — through the other five.

**What I am not doing.** Whether those five should be coupled is a product-contract
decision (PM, with `quant_analyst` on any graded case). I am not making it and I have not
edited the code, PD-0006, or the design. The reviewable facts are: the code permits it,
the design cannot render it, PD-0006 asserts a consistency that does not hold, and
`CP0_RECONCILIATION.md` §1 records the §32 row as "Identical shape, reached separately"
— which was true of the two *planning* artifacts and is no longer true of the shipped
contract.

**Contract violated.** Source PRD §32, P4, P5, P10, §41.3; `specs/FEATURE_PRD.md` §3.4
(a competent stranger cannot execute CP7's rendering from these artifacts as they stand,
because two governing artifacts give contradictory instructions for the same object).
AC-15 itself is **not** violated — see §2, AC-15.

### B-3 — The new test package errors under the repository's canonical suite invocation

**Defect.** `tests/product/` passes only under the bespoke command in its own docstrings
(`PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/product`). Under the invocation
`scripts/self_test.py` step 10 uses — `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'`
— all three product modules fail to import, because `src/` is not on `sys.path` and the
repository has no `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `conftest.py`, or path shim (verified: no
such file exists at root).

**Executed evidence.**

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
ERROR: product.test_methodology_registry (unittest.loader._FailedTest)
ERROR: product.test_metric_result       (unittest.loader._FailedTest)
ERROR: product.test_vocabulary          (unittest.loader._FailedTest)
FAIL:  test_claude_binding.AuthorityIntegrityTests.test_an_authorized_write_whose_status_the_dag_rejects_says_so
FAIL:  test_claude_binding.FailClosedDependencyTests.test_missing_registry_blocks_provenance
Ran 359 tests in 84.303s
FAILED (failures=2, errors=3)
```

**Failure scenario.** The HG1 package must contain reproduction instructions (§38.2). A
reviewer or the owner runs the repository's standard command, sees five red items, and
cannot tell which belong to the increment. `handoff-implement.json` records "Ran full
suite twice: 31/31 passed both times, exit 0" without stating that the result is
invocation-dependent — accurate for the command used, incomplete as a claim about the
repository.

**Attribution, stated precisely so this is not misread:**
- The three **errors** are caused by this increment and are a real regression in
  `scripts/self_test.py` step 10.
- The two **failures** are *not* product defects. `tests/test_claude_binding.py` stages the
  live tree, and both tests encode pre-INC-001 live state as a fixture assumption
  (`test_missing_registry_blocks_provenance` asserts `runtime/executions/implement.json`
  does not exist; it now does, legitimately). This is a harness-test hygiene defect owned
  by `harness_architect`, outside my write authority, recorded here as evidence.

**Contract.** `specs/FEATURE_PRD.md` §12 item 3; source PRD §38.2 (reproduction
instructions). **AC-18 itself is satisfied** — see §2.

### AC-15 — non-`AVAILABLE` state cannot carry a presentable value — **satisfied** (AC's own test), with the enforcement claim overstated

**Executed.** The negative tests exist and pass:
`AC15NegativeTests` covers `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`+value, `LIMITED`+value, +reason_code, and
`LIMITED`+`0.0`. The `0.0` case matters and is right: `__post_init__` tests
`self.value is not None`, not truthiness, so `0.0` and `""` are correctly rejected rather
than passing as "no value." AC-15's stated test — "an automated negative test in
`tests/product/` fails the construction" — is met.

**But the module's docstring claims more than the code delivers:** *"there is no code path
— not construction, not mutation afterward — that produces an invalid instance."* That is
false for at least two ordinary Python paths, and a CP1 engineer who trusts the docstring
will build on an invariant that does not hold. These are **static analysis, not executed**
(see NR-1 — my attempt to run probes was denied by the write guard and I did not route
around it):

| Vector | Expected result | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `dataclasses.replace(m, sufficiency_state=LIMITED)` | **blocked** — `replace()` re-invokes `__init__` → `__post_init__` | CPython `dataclasses` semantics |
| `object.__setattr__(m, "sufficiency_state", LIMITED)` | **hole** — bypasses the frozen `__setattr__` | standard frozen-dataclass escape hatch |
| `object.__new__(MetricResult)` + `object.__setattr__` | **hole** — `__init__`/`__post_init__` never run | — |
| `class Loose(MetricResult)` overriding `__post_init__` to `pass` | **hole**, and the important one — `isinstance(x, MetricResult)` is `True`, no dunder trickery, looks like ordinary code | `MetricResult` is not final; no `__init_subclass__` guard |
| `copy.deepcopy` / `pickle` round-trip of a tampered instance | **propagates** the invalid state — dataclass reduction restores `__dict__` without `__init__` | matters if `MetricResult` is ever persisted/deserialized |

The subclass vector is the one with a plausible CP1 failure scenario: an engineer needs
`MetricResult` plus a freshness field (which is exactly what B-2/§2.3 will push someone to
do), subclasses it, overrides `__post_init__` to add validation, forgets `super().__post_init__()`,
and every AC-15 guarantee silently lapses for the subclass while type checks still pass.
`object.__setattr__` and pickle are the usual Python caveats and I would not call them
defects; the docstring's absolute claim and the missing subclass guard are.

**Also unconstrained: the inverse direction.** `MetricResult(value=None,
sufficiency_state=AVAILABLE)` is permitted and pinned by a test as intended. AC-15 does
not forbid it. But D3.2 renders `AVAILABLE` as "the computed value, in its normal numeric
format" — so an `AVAILABLE` result carrying no value renders as a blank where a number
belongs, which §32 forbids in the same breath as zero and fabricated fallbacks. Failure
scenario: a CP1 analytics function early-returns `MetricResult(None, AVAILABLE)` on a path
its author thought unreachable; the UI shows an empty cell on a metric labelled available.
Non-blocking (N-1), because it is outside AC-15's text — but it is the same class of
defect AC-15 exists to prevent, and it is one line to close.

## 3. Direct answers to the questions referred to this review

### 3.1 Is the engineer's OQ-01 decoupling claim true? (`FEATURE_TECH_PLAN.md` §9)

**The structural claim is true. The risk verdict drawn from it is not supported.**

The claim — a flat-nine resolution is "a field-shape migration inside one entity type …
no module boundary, no service split, and no other T1–T8 decision changes" — holds when I
walk T1–T8 myself:

- **T1** — no boundary moves. The seven splits in §1.3 are drawn on data-ownership and
  trust lines; none is keyed on the state vocabulary. **True.**
- **T3** — `MetricResult` collapses from two fields to one. This is the migration the
  engineer describes. **True.**
- **T4** — control 2's schema definition changes; controls 1, 3, 4 do not. The engineer
  says exactly this. **True.**
- **T5** — §5.2's sentence "surfaces as a `LIMITED`/`INSUFFICIENT_DATA` state" needs
  rewording. Sentence-level. **True.**
- **T6, T7, T8** — untouched. The Computation Manifest and the gate graph are indifferent.
  **True.**

**But the claim is incomplete in a way that understates the cost, and the omission is not
a T1–T8 item, which is why the scoping hid it.** Under a flat nine-value enum, the AC-15
invariant itself has to be re-specified: "non-`AVAILABLE` cannot carry a value" no longer
partitions the space, so someone must decide, for each of the nine, whether it may carry a
presentable value. `STALE_DATA` plausibly may (a stale price is still a number);
`CALCULATION_ERROR` plausibly may not; `MISSING_BENCHMARK` is genuinely arguable — the
designer raises the same question at D3.5 ("should `MISSING_BENCHMARK` still show the
unbenchmarked raw historical values?"). That is nine product-contract decisions requiring
PM and `quant_analyst` input, not a mechanical relabel — and it is a change to the
*invariant*, not to a field's shape.

So the honest summary is the one `CP0_RECONCILIATION.md` §2.1 already reached from a
different direction: *the answer "low risk" is true of the layer the engineer was asked
about and misleading as a project cost.* §9's structural analysis is sound and correctly
bounded; its concluding "[J] I am treating this as low-risk-to-defer" is a verdict the
plan is not positioned to make, because the presentation contract and the invariant are
outside its field of view and it does not say so. The engineer was right to refuse to
self-certify it, and the PM was right to record the divergence rather than average it.

### 3.2 Was the I2 narrowing correct, or convenient?

Correct in premise, over-broad in scope. Full analysis in **B-2**. Short form: keeping
`AVAILABLE` + `STALE_DATA` representable was right and refusing to invent the staleness
threshold was right; declining to couple the *other five* reason codes was not required by
PD-0006 and is contradicted by PD-0006's own text, which supplies the exemption list the
engineer said would have to be invented. Yes, it leaves a hole — `AVAILABLE` + a value +
`MISSING_BENCHMARK`/`CALCULATION_ERROR` is constructible today and renders as a bare
number under D3.2.

### 3.3 Sizing the disclosed freshness gap (`CP0_RECONCILIATION.md` §3.1)

**It is more than a field addition and less than a misplaced boundary. It is a missing
projection, and one specific instruction is missing from the plan.**

The naive fix — add `freshness` and `as_of` to `MetricResult` — is *wrong*, and would
violate the design it is meant to serve. D5.1 requires freshness disclosed **per axis**
(one per listing market, one per FX pair) and forbids merging them; a scalar field on
`MetricResult` is precisely the "single blended indicator" D5.1 prohibits, and a portfolio
metric spanning US + HK equities and two FX pairs has four axes, not one.

The carrier already exists in the plan, unnoticed: the **Computation Manifest** (§6.2)
pins `market_data_snapshot_ref` — "the set of SecurityPrice/FXRate `(source, timestamp)`
pairs actually consumed" — and `fx_series_ref` separately. That is per-axis freshness
information, already at the right granularity, already attached per calculation, and
§3.1's `MetricResult` already names "the T6 computation-context reference" as a field.
So the contract boundary is in roughly the right place.

What is missing is a statement that **the manifest is a display-time dependency, not only
an audit-time one**, plus the derivation rule from pinned timestamps to the D5 freshness
states (`LIVE`/`DELAYED`/`END_OF_DAY`/`STALE`) and the rule that the projection preserves
per-axis granularity through to the claim. As written, §6 frames the manifest purely as
reproduction machinery ("reproduction is: given the same six references…"), and a CP7
engineer reading the plan for "where does the freshness indicator get its data" finds
nothing.

**Size:** a CP1–CP2 specification item (define the projection; decide whether it hangs off
`MetricResult` or off the claim/Insight object), not a CP0 re-architecture. **But** it is
now entangled with **B-2**: PD-0006 moved ordinary staleness onto the D5 axis, the D5 axis
has no route to the claim, and D3.2 refuses to render a reason code on `AVAILABLE`. All
three doors to disclosing "this number is priced off stale data" are currently shut. The
PM was right to disclose this rather than close it, and right that it does not block
`implement`; it should reach the owner at HG1 as one item with B-2, not as two.

### 3.4 Scope compliance (PD-0004, §38.4) — **clean, no finding**

Nothing in `src/` or `tests/product/` is CP1 content — no ledger, positions, cash,
instrument resolution, pricing, FX, corporate actions, benchmarks, or analytic
calculation, and no stub or scaffold for any of them. There is no arithmetic in `src/` at
all. Four files, three of which are enums, one validator, one frozen dataclass. `git status
--porcelain` confirms `src/` and `tests/product/` are the only new implementation paths.
The tech plan implements nothing. This is the cleanest part of the increment and it was
the easiest place to cheat.

## 4. Non-blocking findings

Each has a failure scenario. None blocks the gate package in my judgment; several should
be logged so CP1 does not rediscover them.

**N-1 — `AVAILABLE` with `value=None` has no rendering.** See AC-15 above. §32 forbids
blank renderings; D3.2 gives `AVAILABLE` only a numeric rendering. Constructible and
test-blessed. One-line fix available (`AVAILABLE ⇒ value is not None`) but it is a
contract decision, not mine.

**N-2 — `validate_entry` checks presence, not content.** `{f: None for f in REQUIRED_FIELDS}`
passes. Failure scenario: CP3 registers Sharpe with `formula: null` and
`annualization_convention: null`; the registry accepts it, and §33's consumers — the "See
evidence" view and AI methodology explanations (§33 closing line, P9, FR-032) — render
empty method text behind a real number. The module argues content is `quant_analyst`'s
judgment, which is right about *which* value is correct and wrong about whether *a* value
is required. A non-null/non-empty requirement with an explicit `NOT_APPLICABLE` sentinel
would separate the two. Contract decision — logged, not made.

**N-3 — the registry has no key and no version discipline, which is what T6's
reproducibility actually rests on.** `MethodologyRegistry` accepts any tuple of valid
entries: two entries with the same `metric_name` and the same `implementation_version` and
different formulas can coexist. Plan §6.2 grounds reproducibility on
"MethodologyRegistryEntry versions are immutable once published — a convention change
creates a new version rather than mutating an existing one." Nothing in the shipped schema
enforces uniqueness, immutability, or monotonic versioning. Failure scenario: CP3 corrects
a Sharpe formula in place without bumping the version; every Computation Manifest citing
that version now cites a method that no longer exists, and an audit reproduction silently
returns a different number — NFR-001/NFR-010 broken with no error anywhere. Not required
by AC-16, and I would not build it at CP0; it should be logged as a CP1 requirement
because the plan's determinism argument already depends on it.

**N-4 — a frozen registry of mutable mappings.** `entries: Tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...]`
holds `dict`s, and `validate_entry` runs only at construction. `registry.entries[0].pop("formula")`
leaves a "validated" registry holding an invalid entry. Static analysis, not executed
(NR-1). Same family as the `MetricResult` caveats; worth a `MappingProxyType` or a frozen
entry type at CP1.

**N-5 — "major dependencies" are documented at category level only.** §38.3 asks for
"proposed technology stack and major dependencies." The plan names `decimal.Decimal`,
"`numpy`/`pandas`-class libraries," and mypy, but no dependency inventory. AC-09's stated
test is about boundaries and is met; a stranger cannot derive a manifest from this. Given
no network egress, no inventory could have been validated anyway — reasonable, worth a
sentence at CP1.

**N-6 — the plan promises an artifact `implement` did not deliver.** §2 states the
methodology registry will be "validated against the JSON Schema `implement` will deliver
under `schemas/`." `ls schemas/` shows twenty harness schemas and no methodology schema;
`implement` delivered a Python `REQUIRED_FIELDS` tuple and `validate_entry` instead.
`specs/FEATURE_PRD.md` I3 says "registry schema and validator" without mandating JSON
Schema, so `implement` is within its brief — but a stranger following the plan looks for a
file that does not exist. One of the two documents should be corrected; neither is mine.

**N-7 — an out-of-scope item lost its qualifier in transcription.** Source PRD §5.3 excludes
"complex corporate reorganizations **beyond basic supported events**";
`specs/FEATURE_PRD.md` §4 renders it "complex corporate reorganizations." Failure scenario:
a CP1 engineer reads §4 and concludes corporate actions are out of V1, contradicting §12
("first-class treatment") and CP1's own deliverable list. Small, and exactly the kind of
drift the competent-stranger test is for. (`bonds` for "individual bonds" is harmless.)

**N-8 — the Tool Gateway is called "read-only" but exposes `run_scenario()`.** §22.2's
function list includes `run_scenario()`, and §1.3/§4.1 describe the gateway as read-only.
Scenario Lab is specified to write to its own hypothetical-state store. Failure scenario:
CP9 needs a scenario to persist for follow-up questions; "read-only" gives no rule, so
either the AI-facing surface acquires a write path — the one thing P8's structural
argument depends on it not having — or the capability is silently dropped. Cheap to
resolve now by qualifying "read-only with respect to actual portfolio state; scenario
state is write-isolated." Flagged because P8 is the increment's strongest structural claim
and this is the one loose thread in it.

**N-9 — `value` is the only unvalidated field on `MetricResult`.** `sufficiency_state` and
`reason_code` get `isinstance` checks; `value: Optional[float]` gets none, so an
`AVAILABLE` result can carry `"N/A"`, `float("nan")`, or any object (static analysis, not
executed — NR-1). Control 2 in T4 leans on this envelope being typed. Minor at CP0, worth
closing when `Decimal` arrives (plan §2 proposes `decimal.Decimal` for money, which will
make the `float` annotation wrong anyway).

## 7. Known limitations of this review

1. **My strongest findings are unexecutable.** B-1 and B-2 are arguments about
   specifications and type contracts. A reader is entitled to disagree with B-1's judgment
   that "material" is undecidable — that is a judgment, though the three cases in B-1a are
   concrete. B-2 is closer to fact: the constructibility of `AVAILABLE` + value +
   `MISSING_BENCHMARK` follows from code I read, and D3.2's sentence is quoted verbatim.
2. **NR-1 leaves the AC-15 escape-hatch analysis unexecuted.** If the subclass vector
   matters to the decision, someone with write authority in `tests/` should run it rather
   than take my word.
3. **I reviewed the tech plan against the source PRD, not against the state of the art.**
   I did not evaluate whether a modular monolith, PostgreSQL, or Python is the *best*
   choice — only whether the choices are explicit, reasoned, and logged where open
   (AC-13's actual bar). ADR-P1/P2/P3 are HG1's to judge on merit.
4. **I did not verify the design artifact, the increment PRD as a whole, or the harness
   state machine.** AC-01 is included only because its own test text assigns it to me.
5. **One reviewer, one pass.** I attacked hardest at the places named in my dispatch, which
   means the places nobody named are the least examined — principally T7's dependency graph
   beyond the §38.5 reproduction, and the ADR proposals' individual merits.
6. **Attribution risk on B-3's two `test_claude_binding` failures.** I read both tests and
   believe they fail on live-state fixture assumptions rather than on anything this
   increment did wrong. I did not bisect against a pre-INC-001 tree to prove it.
7. **This review is not an approval and cannot become one.** Passing tests, my findings,
   elapsed time, and absence of objection are never HG1 (source PRD §38.1, §44.23;
   `CLAUDE.md`). If this document is cited as evidence that the increment is *approved*,
   it is being misread.

## 13.2 B-1's mechanism: does provenance-bound rendering earn AC-10?

**The design is a real answer, and I want to say that before I attack it.** The old
Control 3 asked "is this generated number acceptable?", which is a judgment. The new one
changes what the AI is permitted to *emit*: a template of prose plus
`{{slot: tool_call_id, field_path}}` citations, resolved and formatted by a deterministic
Rendering Service on the trusted side. The AI never writes the digits that reach the user
for any cited value. That inverts the problem from *detecting* bad output to *structurally
preventing* one class of it, and it removes the pressure I warned about in round 1: a
false rejection can no longer be relieved by loosening a numeric-equivalence rule, because
there is no numeric-equivalence rule. §4.0's three-route decomposition is the right frame,
Control 2's demotion to "a P5 control, not a P1 control" is the correct self-correction,
and Control 4's rescoping to "route 1 only, defense-in-depth, not part of the count" is
honest. §4.5 logs residuals instead of claiming closure, and §11 explicitly refuses to
self-certify AC-10 and routes it here. None of that is theatre.

**Now the attack the PM asked for.**

### Does it block my worked example, or relocate it?

For the exact string I used — "you beat your benchmark by **2.3** percentage points" — it
blocks it, and I can describe the failure: `2.3` matches `-?\d+\.\d+`, it sits in free
text rather than a resolved slot, the render is rejected and logged. The structural answer
that follows ("call `compare_benchmark()`, which computes on the deterministic side and
returns its own citable field") is correct and is exactly where the arithmetic belongs.

For the same claim one word different, it does not block it. See **B-4**.

### Can a false claim be assembled entirely from true citations?

**Yes, and this residual is not in §4.5's list.** The Rendering Service validates that a
slot's `tool_call_id` and `field_path` exist and resolves the value verbatim. Nothing
validates that the *free text around the slot* describes what that field actually is. The
AI writes the label, the entity, the period, and the unit; the trusted side writes only
the digits.

Failure scenario, entirely within the sanctioned path: the AI calls `calculate_risk()`
twice, once for a 1-year window and once for 3-year. It then emits
`"Your **3-year** beta is {{slot: call_7, value}}"` where `call_7` is the **1-year** call.
Every digit is verbatim from a logged tool call. No numeric token appears in free text. The
render succeeds. The user reads a false 3-year beta, and the audit trail says it was
grounded — because the *value* was.

This is not §4.5's residual 1 (qualitative mischaracterization *without a number*): this
claim has a number, and its number is correct in isolation. It is a distinct third residual
— **provenance binds values, not the claims they sit inside**. It is arguably outside
AC-10's literal text (nothing was *originated*), but it is inside §22.3's requirement that
a material numerical claim be grounded, and inside §41.4. The shape of the gap is that
slots carry a value but not the identity of what was measured; the fix is the engineer's
to design, not mine to specify. Logged as **N-10**, non-blocking, and recommended for
§4.5's list — because §4.5 presents itself as the enumeration of what is not solved, and
an enumeration that is missing its most dangerous member misleads by omission.

### Are §4.5's two logged residuals the right two?

Residual 1 (qualitative mischaracterization) is real, correctly characterized, and
correctly routed toward Insight Engine severity rather than a T4 control.

Residual 2 (numbers spelled out in words, "two point three") is real but **its reasoning
does not survive**, and that is what surfaces B-4. The plan argues the case is acceptable
because a written-out number "reads as obviously anomalous prose in a data-driven UI." That
is plausible for *"two point three"*. It is false for its immediate neighbour, *"2
percentage points"* — which the value-shape definition also permits, which is not anomalous
prose at all, and which §4.5 does not mention. The residual was logged one notch too far
out; the case just inside it is the dangerous one.

### Two destinations, asymmetric trust

Holds. See §13.1's B-1b row. The one thing it correctly declines to solve — that prompt
text sent to a hosted provider may contain already-fetched portfolio values, a data-handling
matter for §41.1/§41.2 rather than for P1 — is routed to the right risk log rather than
manufactured into a control. That is the correct disposition.

## 13.3 B-4 and B-5 — the two new blocking findings

### B-4 (blocking) — the value-shape definition is decidable but under-inclusive, and route 2 survives in the phrasing the product itself demands

**Defect.** §4.3a defines a value-shaped token as: a decimal `-?\d+\.\d+`; a number
immediately followed by `%`; a number with a currency symbol or ISO code; or a
comma-grouped integer of 4+ digits. It then states explicitly that **a bare integer with
none of those markers is "deliberately not value-shaped, and therefore not blocked as free
text,"** justified by ordinals ("top 3 holdings"), tenor ("5-year window") and years
("2026"). The justification covers those three cases. The exemption covers far more.

**Failure scenario — my round-1 example, unmodified in substance.** Tool calls return
`0.0840` and `0.0610`. The AI emits, as free text with no slot:

> "You're up about **8 percent** versus **6 percent** for the benchmark — you beat it by
> roughly **2 percentage points**."

Walk it through §4.3a: `8`, `6`, `2` are bare integers; none is immediately followed by
`%` (the unit is the *word* "percent"); none has a currency marker; none is comma-grouped;
none matches `\d+\.\d+`. **No value-shaped token is present. The render is accepted.** An
AI-originated derived number reaches the user, which is precisely what P1, §22.3, §41.4 and
CP9's exit criterion forbid, and precisely what B-1 was raised about.

**Why this is not an exotic evasion.** It requires no adversarial intent. Source PRD §22.7
and the design's D2 require the product to render claims at **Quick** and **Simple** depth
levels in plainer language — and "up about 8 percent" *is* the plain-language rendering of
`0.0840`. The mechanism is therefore weakest in exactly the two of four depth levels where
the product mandates the phrasing that evades it. Nothing pushes the model toward `8.40%`;
the product pushes it away.

**The structural point, stated once.** The predicate's polarity is the defect. It is a
**blocklist of number shapes**, so it is under-inclusive by construction and fails open on
anything not enumerated — bare integers, word units ("percent", "percentage points",
"basis points", "dollars"), and any future formatting nobody listed. An allowlist polarity
("no digit may appear in free text except in these enumerated non-claim forms") is
decidable by the same mechanical standard, fails closed, and its false rejections push the
direction §4.3a itself argues is the safe one — toward adding a Tool Gateway field. Which
polarity to adopt, and how to enumerate the non-claim forms, is `engineer`'s call and
HG1's to approve. I am naming the defect and its direction, not writing the rule.

**Contract violated.** `specs/FEATURE_PRD.md` AC-10; source PRD P1, §22.3, NFR-002, §41.4;
CP9 exit criterion. **AC-10: not satisfied.**

**Proportion, stated so this is not read as round 1 repeated.** Round 1 found no control
against route 2 at all and an undefined term at the centre of the one that claimed to be.
Round 2 finds a real control with a mechanical predicate whose coverage boundary is drawn
one notch too permissively. That is a different order of defect, and if the PM's judgment
is to carry it to the owner as a disclosed residual rather than close it first, that is a
defensible call — provided AC-10 is reported **not satisfied** and §4.5 names the case.

### B-5 (blocking, and the cheapest finding in this review) — the Rendering Service is not in the architecture

**Defect.** §4.3 introduces the Rendering Service as a trusted backend component that is
"the only thing that turns a template into displayed text." Every P1 guarantee in the
reworked plan passes through it. It appears in T1 **nowhere**:

- §1.2's bounded-context diagram is unchanged and still reads "AI Orchestration: separate
  module …, calls Tool Gateway only," with no rendering stage between the AI and the client;
- §1.3's boundary table has no `AI Orchestration vs Rendering Service` row — and that is now
  the single most important trust boundary in the system;
- §1.4's dependency rules do not place it;
- §12's declared-deviations list still says "**No other deviation** from source PRD content
  is claimed," while the plan has in fact added a fourth component absent from §37 — on
  exactly the same footing as the three amendments §12 does declare.

**Failure scenario.** A competent stranger implements T1 at CP1/CP7 — the module structure,
the API surface, the dependency rules — and builds no Rendering Service, because the
architecture does not contain one. AI response text is wired from AI Orchestration to the
client through the API layer, which is what §1.2 draws. At CP9 the P1 mechanism has to be
retrofitted into a response path that already exists, which is the retrofit ADR-P4 itself
says costs "re-auditing every AI code path."

**Why it is blocking despite being an editorial fix.** By the plan's own standard: §1.1
item 2 argues the Tool Gateway had to be *drawn* because "T4 depends on it existing as a
drawn boundary, not an internal convention." The Rendering Service now carries more of T4
than the Tool Gateway does, and it is an internal convention. And §38.2 requires the gate
package to declare deviations from source material; §12 currently asserts completeness that
is no longer true. T1 and §12 are what HG1 approves.

**Contract violated.** AC-09 ("each major boundary states what is on each side and why");
source PRD §38.2, §38.3 (architecture and service boundaries documented).

"3-year beta" label, fully grounded, fully wrong. Recommended for §4.5's residual list.

`MetricResult` entity still reads "a state (§32 — shape depends on OQ-01, see §9 below)."
Failure scenario: a stranger reads §9 and §10, concludes the state vocabulary is unsettled
and the old grounding-check design is current, and re-opens a decision PD-0006 closed. Note
that the same §8.2 table's AI-provider row *was* correctly updated, so this is uneven

**N-12 — The replacement enforcement claim is narrower than the original and still one
vector wide.** Round 1's claim was false; the replacement — "ordinary code — construction,
assignment, subclassing, `replace`, `copy`, `pickle` — cannot produce an invalid
`MetricResult`. Code that deliberately reaches for `object.__setattr__` or `object.__new__`
can" — is a real improvement and is right about every vector it names. It is under-inclusive
by one: a frozen dataclass without `__slots__` still exposes a writable instance `__dict__`,
so `m.__dict__["sufficiency_state"] = SufficiencyState.LIMITED` produces an invalid instance
without touching either named method. Same family, same severity, no fix needed at CP0 — the
caveat's *characterization* is what wants widening, to something like "any code that reaches
past the type's public interface." **Static analysis, not executed** (NR2-1); no test covers
this vector.

## 14.2 AC-10 — the allowlist, attacked

### Does it close my sentence in both forms?

**Yes.** I evaluated it by hand against all four exemptions rather than accepting the
claim (E3-1).

*Digit form* — "You're up about **8 percent** versus **6 percent** … by roughly **2
percentage points**." Each of `8`, `6`, `2` is a digit in free text, so each must clear an
exemption. Form 1 (ticker): requires letters glued to the digits with no space — "8
percent" has a space. Form 2 (year): requires four digits in 1900–2099. Form 3
(ordinal/count): requires "top/bottom/first/last" immediately before, or one of six
structural nouns immediately after — "percent" is not among them. Form 4 (tenor): requires
a hyphen plus year/month/week/day/quarter. **All four fail for all three digits. Rejected.**

*Word form* — "up about **eight** percent … by roughly **two** percentage points."
"eight" and "two" are in the closed cardinal vocabulary; forms 1, 2 and 4 are digit-shaped
and cannot match a word; form 3 is explicitly narrowed to the digit form (the plan
discloses this asymmetry and accepts the resulting false rejection of "top three
holdings"). **Rejected.**

The polarity is now right, and the plan's argument for why it stays right — that reducing
false rejections means *adding to a reviewable enumeration*, not turning a numeric-tolerance
dial — is sound. That was the specific failure mode I warned about in round 2 and it is
structurally unavailable now.

### Is the vocabulary's incompleteness fatal, or an acceptable disclosed residual?

**Acceptable as a residual — but the disclosure understates it, and its stated rationale
contains a false premise.**

§4.3a argues that unit and quantity words ("percent", "points", "basis points", "times",
"fold", "x") need not be enumerated "because the number next to them would be caught."
That reasoning holds only where the number is a separate token. It fails for **fused
number-unit words**, where there is no adjacent number to catch:

- "your HK exposure is **twice** your US exposure" — "twice" is not a cardinal
  (`two` is; `twice` is not), not an ordinal, not a fraction, not a scale word;
- "your tech sleeve **doubled** this year" — same, and "tripled", "halved" likewise;
- "you hold a **dozen** technology positions" — "dozen" is a number word and is on none
  of the four sub-lists.

Each states a quantity with no digit and no listed word. §4.5's disclosure names the risk
as "a number word not on the list, e.g. a regional English variant or a compound this plan
did not anticipate" — these are not regional variants; they are core English, and they are
omitted because the omission *rationale* has a hole, not because someone forgot a rare
word.

**Why it is still not fatal.** A closed vocabulary that is wrong is genuinely different
from a blocklist that is open by construction, and the difference is not rhetorical: every
digit-bearing expression — which is how a language model writing financial prose states a
figure the overwhelming majority of the time — is rejected by default and must clear a named
exemption. The word-form gap is a bounded list-completeness problem, closable by adding
entries, reviewable line by line at CP9. **It is the acceptable kind.** What I would not
accept is the disclosure as written, because it points at the wrong cause. See N-15.

**One decidability question the rule does not answer:** whether vocabulary matching is
whole-token or substring. Substring is untenable ("one" occurs inside "money", "component",
"zone"); whole-token lets fused compounds through ("twofold", "tenfold", "half-yearly").
The plan does not say which, and that choice changes what the control catches. Recorded in
N-15 as a specification gap, not a defect in the design.

### Do the four exempted forms leak? Yes — three of them, with ordinary examples

This is where I spent most of round 3, and it is the round's main yield.

**Form 1 (ticker fragments) has no adjacency guard, and it exempts digit-unit shorthand.**
The rule exempts "a digit run … immediately followed by `.HK`, `.SS`, `.SZ`, `.US`, or 1–4
uppercase letters with no separating space." That shape is not only tickers. It is also:

> "your tracking error widened by **250BP**" · "cash of about **12M**" · "the HK sleeve
> returned **3X** the US sleeve" · "**8K** in dividends"

`250BP`, `12M`, `3X`, `8K` each match "digit run + 1–4 uppercase letters, no space" and are
therefore exempted as ticker fragments. These are exactly the **fused number-unit forms**
the vocabulary section assumed away — the same blind spot arriving through the other door.
Note the asymmetry that makes this diagnosable as an oversight rather than a decision: Form
2 *was* given an adjacency guard (no currency symbol, `%`, or number-word beside it); Form 1
was given none.

**Form 2 (calendar years) exempts any bare four-digit integer in 1900–2099.** Its guard
excludes adjacency to a currency symbol, `%`, or a number-word — which catches "2026%" and
"2026 dollars", both of which the plan names. It does not catch a bare figure that happens
to fall in the year range:

> "the Hang Seng closed at **1950**" · "your position is worth **1975**"

Index levels, share prices and portfolio values sit in 1900–2099 routinely. Nothing about
"closed at 1950" trips the guard, and an index level is a market fact the deterministic
side owns.

**Form 3 (ordinal/count phrases) exempts counts of the user's own portfolio, by design.**
Its six structural nouns are `holdings`, `positions`, `accounts`, `listings`, `currencies`,
`markets` — every one of them a *portfolio* noun. "top 3 holdings" is a safe selector; but
the same rule exempts:

> "you hold **7 positions** in technology" · "spread across **5 accounts**" · "**3
> currencies**"

Those are counts of the user's own data — portfolio facts the deterministic engine owns and
that P1 says the AI must not originate. **This is the most consequential of the five**,
because it is not an oversight: the rule was written to permit exactly this shape. Whether a
holdings count is a "material portfolio number" requiring a slot is a product decision, and
it is one the owner can take by reading four bullet points. It should be put to them
explicitly rather than inherited from a rule about ordinals.

**Form 4 (tenor descriptors)** I could not make leak. Its scoping — unbound tenors only,
with slot-adjacent tenors deferred to §4.3b's label binding — is careful, and it is
explicitly written to avoid re-opening N-10. Note that "a quarter of your portfolio" is
correctly *not* exempt: "quarter" is a fraction word and form 4 requires an integer-hyphen
shape, so the quantity claim is rejected. That is the rule working.

### So: is AC-10 satisfied?

**Yes.** AC-10 asks whether the plan names a specific mechanism, whether it is structural
rather than a guideline, and whether a reviewer can describe how a violation would fail. All
three are met: the mechanism is provenance-bound rendering with label binding, behind a
fail-closed free-text rule, with credential isolation and an import lint on the other route;
nothing in it is "the prompt tells the model not to"; and I can describe the failure path
precisely — free text containing a digit or a listed number-word that clears no enumerated
exemption is rejected at render time, logged as a grounding violation, before display.

**What "satisfied" does not mean.** It does not mean the residuals are gone. Five ways an
AI-originated number can still reach a user are listed in §14.4. My reason for calling AC-10
satisfied anyway is in §14.3, and I would rather be argued out of it than have it read as
inattention.

## 14.3 Why I stopped here, stated so it can be challenged

Three rounds, and each round I found a defect in the same control. That pattern can mean two
things and the difference matters: either the artifact keeps failing, or the defects keep
getting smaller. They keep getting smaller, and the shape of each is different in kind:

| Round | Defect | Class | Cost to close |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No control existed for the derived-arithmetic route; the one that claimed to cover it turned on an undefined word | **Missing mechanism** | Design a mechanism |
| 2 | Mechanism present and structurally right; its enforcing predicate was a blocklist, open by construction, exempting the phrasing the product's own depth model mandates | **Wrong polarity** | Redesign the predicate |
| 3 | Polarity right, default is reject; three of four enumerated exemptions are drawn wider than their stated purpose, and one word list has a hole | **Enumeration too wide** | Edit four bullet points |

A round-3 defect cannot be fixed by a runtime dial and cannot be argued away at
implementation time: every one of them is a line in a list that a reviewer reads. That is the
property the engineer claimed for the allowlist and it is true. It is also the property that
makes these safe to carry to a gate: the owner can see them, and CP9's implementation review
will read the same four bullets again with real code beside them.

**The line I drew:** a defect blocks if the owner would be *misled* by the artifact or if the
next increment could not be executed from it. Neither holds now. B-5 blocked because the
architecture omitted its own P1 mechanism while §12 asserted completeness — the owner would
have approved a diagram that was false. §14.4's five are disclosed defects in a rule the
owner can read, provided they travel. **If the PM's judgment is that the form-3 portfolio-count
exemption should be closed before the gate rather than decided at it, that is a defensible
call and I would not argue against it.** I did not make it a blocker because it is a product
decision about what counts as a material number, and that decision is the owner's, not mine
and not the engineer's.

## 14.4 New non-blocking findings (round 3)

**N-13 — §1.3 and §4.3b specify two different label mechanisms, and only one closes N-10.**
This is the PM's question — does `label_ref` close it or relocate it — and the answer is
that the plan says both.

- **§1.3's boundary row:** the Rendering Service "renders the label from **the cited
  call's** `MethodologyRegistryEntry`." Derived on the trusted side. The AI cannot mismatch.
  N-10 closed.
- **§4.3b:** the slot "carries a third component, `label_ref`, naming the
  `MethodologyRegistryEntry` … The Rendering Service renders the label text itself … from
  **that registry entry's** `metric_name` plus the cited call's pinned window parameter."
  Here `label_ref` is authored by the AI alongside `tool_call_id`, and nothing states that
  the Service checks `label_ref` against the entry the cited `MetricResult` actually
  references.

Under §4.3b's reading the window is trusted (which is why my exact 1-year/3-year example is
closed) but **metric identity is still AI-chosen**: cite `label_ref` = the Sharpe Ratio entry
with `field_path` pointing at a beta value and the display reads "Sharpe Ratio (1-year)" over
a beta. Failure scenario complete, no free-text number involved, §4.3a has nothing to scan.

The resolution is one line and the plan already contains it: **§3.1's `MetricResult` carries
its own `methodology_ref` (registry ID + version)**, so the authoritative binding exists on
the trusted side and §1.3's reading is implementable today. Which of the two readings is
intended is the engineer's to state; I am reporting that the document currently says both.

**N-14 — the provenance repair is honest about `engineer-01` and incomplete about
`engineer-02`.** `exec-tech-planning-002`'s note preserves `engineer-01`'s T1–T8 authorship
explicitly and explains the single-record overwrite — that part is exactly right, and it is
the part that was at risk. But the note's scope description covers only the round-2 rework
(§4, §8.1/8.2, §10, §11). The round-3 work now in the artifact — §1.1–§1.4, §3.1, §4.3a's
allowlist, §4.3b, §4.5, §9, §12 — is described nowhere in any execution record. A reader
reconciling the file against `runtime/executions/tech_planning.json` finds no record covering
the majority of what is currently in it. Provenance hygiene, `engineer`/`product_manager` to
resolve; the readiness validator does not check note completeness (it passed — E3-5).

**N-15 — §4.5's residual list is again missing members, and residual 2's cause is
misdiagnosed.** §4.5 was revised specifically because "an enumeration of what is unsolved
that omits its most dangerous member misleads by omission." It now discloses one of the five
residuals in §14.2. It omits the three exemption leaks (forms 1, 2, 3), attributes the
word-vocabulary gap to "regional English variants" rather than to the false premise that unit
words need not be listed, and does not resolve the whole-token-vs-substring matching question.
Same shape of finding as round 2's, one level down.

**N-16 — the form-3 portfolio-count exemption is a product decision presented as a
grammatical one.** Split out from §14.2 because it is the one item here that is not an
engineering oversight: the six structural nouns are all portfolio nouns, so the rule
deliberately permits the AI to originate counts of the user's own holdings, positions,
accounts, listings, currencies and markets. Recommend it be put to the owner at HG1 as an
explicit question — *must a portfolio count be slot-cited like any other portfolio number?* —
rather than settled inside a rule about ordinals.

## 14.6 The canonical-suite failure count — the PM's question 4

**I observe 5, twice, in this round; 401 tests, 0 errors.** The engineer reports 6 this
pass; the PM observed 5 and, earlier, 6.

**What I verified:** every one of the five is a `self.staged(td)` test that copies the live
tree into a temp directory and asserts against pre-delivery values. Two of them
(`test_producer_cannot_forge_reviewer_provenance`, `test_P2_an_unregistered_worker_is_refused_rather_than_recorded_blank`)
assert that `runtime/executions/technical_review.json` does **not** exist — it exists
because I wrote it. A third asserts the same for `implement`. A fourth depends on DAG state
that INC-001 advanced; the fifth compares `PACK_CHECKSUMS.sha256` against a tree that keeps
gaining delivery artifacts. **No harness test imports `product_contract`** (round-2 E2-5,
still true: `grep -rl` returns zero files), and no product test is in the failure set in any
observation by any observer.

**On whether the count moved for that reason and not another: the mechanism is confirmed,
the specific sixth is not.** The count is a function of *live mutable state at the moment of
the run*, and the state changed between the engineer's run and mine in at least one way I can
name precisely — **I set `state/tasks/technical_review.json` to `in_progress` at the start of
this round**, having left it `complete` at the end of round 2, and several of these tests
stage and assert against shard status. That is a sufficient mechanism for a 6→5 move. It is
not proof that it *is* the cause, because the sixth failure is passing now and I cannot see
what I cannot run. **Recorded `not_run`:** reconstructing the engineer's tree state would
require staging it as of that run, which I cannot do read-only (NR3-2). What I can say
without qualification is the part that matters — no product code is implicated in any
observation, and 0 errors is stable.

## 14.8 Round-3 limitations

1. **AC-10 rests on my judgment, not on execution.** §14.3 states the reasoning for calling
   it satisfied with five disclosed residuals, in a form the PM can reject. If the owner's
   risk posture is that any residual path to an AI-originated number blocks, then AC-10 is
   not satisfied under that posture and my §14.4 list is the evidence for it. I have given
   the reasoning rather than only the conclusion so the disagreement can be had.
2. **My leak examples are hand-derived, not exhaustive.** I found three leaking exemptions by
   reading four rules adversarially for roughly the time it takes to write fourteen test
   strings. A fourth reader would likely find more. That is an argument for CP9 implementation
   review reading them again, not for holding CP0.
3. **N-13 is a reading of two passages that disagree.** If the engineer intends §1.3's
   version, N-13 is a documentation fix; if §4.3b's, it is a design gap. I cannot tell which
   from the artifact, which is the finding.
4. **I did not re-verify the increment as a whole** (NR3-6), and I have now read this plan
   four times, which makes me a poor judge of whether it reads clearly to someone reading it
   once. The competent-stranger test is the one I am least able to apply by round 3.
5. **Three rounds with the same reviewer.** My round-3 attention went where my own round-2
   findings pointed. The parts of the increment no finding has ever touched — T7's dependency
   graph beyond the §38.5 reproduction, ADR-P1/P2/P3/P5/P6 on their merits — have had one pass
   in round 1 and none since.
6. **Still not an approval.** Clear-to-gate is a statement that a human can now usefully
   review this. It is not a statement that the human should approve it, and it is not one I am
   permitted to make.

**Why B-6 blocks rather than travels.** It is the third instance of the defect class I
have now flagged in three consecutive rounds — a correction landing in one section and not
its neighbour (N-11, then N-13, now this). The difference is what the stale sentence says:
N-11's were stale *references*; this is an affirmative statement of a **superseded

be misled, or could the next increment not be executed from this." Both fail here: an

## 15.1 The AC-15 inversion (delta 1)

### Is the ruling correct? Yes, and one point in its favour it does not claim

PD-0007's three arguments hold. The first is decisive on its own: a `LIMITED` that can
never carry a value renders identically to `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`, which makes the three-state
vocabulary a two-state vocabulary with a redundant label, contradicting PD-0006's own
definitions (*computable* vs *not computable*).

**A fourth argument, which I checked in the source and PD-0007 does not cite:** source PRD
**§9.3** enumerates what is available without cost basis and heads the other list
*"**Unavailable/limited** without cost basis or transaction history: investor-specific
unrealized gain; realized gain; exact money-weighted return…"* The source PRD itself uses
"limited" for a degraded-but-real case and distinguishes it from "unavailable" in the same
breath. Under the old AC-15 that distinction was unrepresentable. PD-0007 does not merely
fix D3.2; it restores a distinction §9.3 already draws.

**On the counter-argument PD-0007 raises against itself** — that correcting an AC in the
permissive direction late is how guarantees get weakened — the discipline is real and it
held: `INSUFFICIENT_DATA ⇒ value is None` remains machine-enforced, and the `LIMITED`
rendering is not bare (D3.2 requires a non-dismissible qualifier in the same visual unit,
never a tooltip). **I do not think you got PD-0007 wrong.**

### Is the invariant what PD-0007 says, and no more? Yes

`__post_init__` now tests `sufficiency_state is INSUFFICIENT_DATA and value is not None`.
Nothing else changed: the PD-0006 five-code frozenset is byte-identical in membership, the
`STALE_DATA` exemption is intact, and `__init_subclass__` and `__reduce__` are untouched
(E4-1). No scope creep, no incidental tightening.

### Was any prior coverage weakened by the retargeting? No — and two vectors got stronger

This was the part you most wanted checked. I traced every test that used "non-`AVAILABLE`
forbids a value" as its negative target (E4-2):

| Test | Old target | Now | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_dataclasses_replace_revalidates_and_blocks_invalid_result` | `AVAILABLE→LIMITED` keeping a value | `AVAILABLE→INSUFFICIENT_DATA` keeping a value | **Retargeted, not deleted.** Still proves `replace()` re-runs `__post_init__` |
| `test_deepcopy_of_a_tampered_instance_revalidates_and_raises` | `LIMITED` + tampered value | `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` + tampered value | Retargeted; `__reduce__` coverage intact |
| `test_pickle_of_a_tampered_instance_revalidates_and_raises_on_load` | same | same | Retargeted; intact |
| `test_object_setattr_bypasses_…` | `LIMITED` + 99.0 | `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` + 99.0 | **Strengthened.** Under PD-0007 the old target is a *valid* object, so had it been left alone this test would have silently stopped demonstrating anything |
| `test_dict_mutation_bypasses_…` | `LIMITED`→`AVAILABLE`, value `None` | `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` + a value | **Strengthened.** The round-3 version produced a *valid* end state and only showed `__dict__` writes bypass `frozen`; it now demonstrably produces an invalid object |
| `test_object_new_bypasses_…` | already `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` | unchanged | Correctly untouched |
| `test_zero_is_still_a_presentable_value_and_is_rejected` | `LIMITED` + `0.0` | `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` + `0.0` | Retargeted; the `is not None` (not truthiness) discipline still pinned, and a *new* `test_limited_with_zero_value` pins the inverted case |
| `ReasonCodeCouplingNegativeTests` (both) | `AVAILABLE` + each of five, ± value | unchanged | PD-0006 negative coverage untouched |

Count reconciles exactly: 45 − 1 (`test_limited_with_value_fails`, correctly removed —
it pinned the wrong rule) + 4 new positives = **48** (E4-3). Nothing was deleted to make a
suite pass, and the one deletion is the test PD-0007 exists to invert.

### One thing PD-0007 opened that PD-0007 does not discuss — N-17

Permitting `LIMITED` to carry a value newly permits it to carry a value **alongside one of
PD-0006's five "cannot be properly computed" reason codes**, and a test now asserts that
combination constructs. For four of the five that is right, and §9.3 above proves it for
`MISSING_COST_BASIS`. For one it is not:

```python
MetricResult(value=1.30, sufficiency_state=LIMITED, reason_code=CALCULATION_ERROR)
```

Constructible today. Rendered under D3.2's `LIMITED` row it reads as the value plus a
qualifier naming its reason code — *"1.30 — calculation error."* A metric whose calculation
errored, presenting a number. Under the old rule this was unreachable; PD-0007 unblocked it
as a side effect.

**This is the same shape as round 1's B-2, in the opposite direction** — a reason code
paired with a state that contradicts it, created by a correction whose blast radius was not
enumerated. It is **not blocking**, and the distinction from B-2 is precise: B-2 produced a
*bare, unqualified* number with no reference point (P4, §41.3); this produces a number
carrying a mandatory visible qualifier naming the error. Disclosed, not silent. Whether
`CALCULATION_ERROR` should be coupled to `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` the way the other four are not
is a one-line product decision, and it is yours, not mine.

## 15.2 The three form leaks (delta 2) — all three closed

I re-ran my string battery against the corrected rules rather than accepting the closure
claim (E4-4).

**Form 1 — closed.** The `1–4 uppercase letters` branch is gone; a digit run must now be
followed by a **literal period** and one of `HK`/`SS`/`SZ`/`US`. `250BP`, `12M`, `3X`, `8K`
all fail it and are rejected. `9988.HK`, `601398.SS` still clear. I could not construct a
fused-unit token that survives: `1.5M` fails (suffix not enumerated), `2.3` fails. The
narrowing to dotless tickers is disclosed as a narrowing rather than presented as free.

**Form 2 — my two examples are closed; the new guard admits one of its own (N-19).**
"closed at 1950" and "worth 1975" are now rejected — "at" and "worth" are not
calendar-context markers. Correct. But the marker list includes **`by`** and **`through`**,
and both are ambiguous between a calendar sense and a magnitude sense:

> "your position grew **by 1950**" · "the index fell **through 2000**"

`1950` is a bare 4-digit integer in range, immediately preceded by an enumerated marker,
with no currency symbol, `%`, or number-word adjacent. **Exempt.** And "increased/grew/fell
**by** N" is the canonical English for a *delta* — route 2, derived arithmetic, the exact
failure class this control exists for. Narrower than my round-3 leaks (it needs the
unpunctuated four-digit form; `$1,950` and `1,950` are both correctly rejected), but real,
and it sits in the guard added to close the previous leak. §4.3a already discloses a
*coincidental* overlap ("since 1975 shares are worth more"); this is not coincidence, it is
a marker doing double duty.

**Form 3 — closed, and correctly.** "you hold 7 positions", "5 accounts", "12 holdings",
"3 currencies" are all rejected; only the `top`/`bottom`/`first`/`last` selector branch
survives. This matches PD-0008's ruling exactly.

**Form 4 — unchanged, still tight.** I could not break it in round 3 or round 4.

**Vocabulary and matching (delta 5).** `dozen` added; the fused multiplier family
(`twice`, `double(d)`, `triple(d)`, `quadruple(d)`, `halve(d)`, and the `-fold` compounds)
enumerated; whole-token matching specified explicitly, with its cost disclosed rather than
hidden (a fused compound not on the list still evades). §4.5's diagnosis is corrected from
"regional variants" to the fused-word cause, which is the real one. **N-15 closed.**

## 15.3 PD-0008 (delta 3) — the ruling is right; one edge inside its own disclosed gap

**The implemented split matches the ruling.** Selector branch exempt, structural-noun
branch removed entirely. Verified against the rule text and by evaluating both phrase
families (E4-4).

**Is the ruling itself right? Yes.** "Does the number assert something about the portfolio
that could be false?" is the correct axis — it is about origination, not about which
arithmetic produced the number, which is exactly what P1 is about. I would not change it.

**One edge, and it falls inside PD-0008's own disclosed limitation (N-20).** A selector can
carry an implicit existence claim when it exceeds reality:

> "your **top 10 holdings** account for most of your risk" — for a portfolio with 7 holdings

The digit selects, but it also asserts that at least ten holdings exist, and that is
falsifiable. So the operative *test* is slightly broader than the *rule* it produced.
PD-0008 anticipates this — *"a phrase that is genuinely ambiguous should fail closed and be
surfaced, not guessed"* — and routes pattern work to CP9. I am recording the concrete
instance so CP9 has it, not reopening the ruling.

## 15.4 N-13 (delta 4) — closed, and closed the right way

`label_ref` is gone from the slot: `{{slot: tool_call_id, field_path}}`, two components.
The Rendering Service reads the label off the cited call's **own** `methodology_ref` and
its Computation Manifest parameters — the same trusted object the value came from — so the
AI no longer chooses which registry entry backs a label. My Sharpe-label-over-a-beta-value
scenario is not constructible through this mechanism.

**§4.3b and §1.3 now agree**, which was the actual finding. I compared them clause by clause
(E4-5): both specify the two-component slot, both specify derivation from the cited call's
own metadata, both say "never from anything the AI supplied." All seven surviving `label_ref`
mentions are annotations of the removal or history of the defect; none is live specification.
Confirmed.

The engineer chose the §1.3 reading — the trusted-derivation one — which is the stronger of
the two. Note the dependency this creates: §4.3b now rests on `MetricResult.methodology_ref`
being populated deterministically. §3.1 declares that field, and `metric_state.py` correctly
excludes it from the CP0 type with a stated reason (no computation exists yet). Consistent.
It also means §3.1 is now load-bearing for this fix while simultaneously being wrong about
AC-15 — see B-6.

# ROUND 5 — Final narrow check (2026-09-05)

**Reviewer:** `review-01`, same independent identity, same write confinement.
**Scope:** B-6 and its neighbour fix; `PD-0007`'s **amendment** making AC-15 a total
equivalence (R-15 / BF-4), which I had not seen; and the round-4 handoff gap. Rounds 1–4
unedited. Out of scope by instruction and not reopened: N-17/NF-5, N-19, N-20, N-18.

## 16.0 Round 5 verdict

> ### CLEAR TO GATE — it stands.
>
> **B-6 is closed**, and the neighbour fix is right and was the correct catch.
> **The total equivalence is correct, correctly implemented, and — for the first time in
> this increment — produces an exact bijection between what the contract can construct
> and what `designs/FEATURE_DESIGN.md` §D3.2 can render.** It creates no state the design
> cannot render and forbids none the design specifies.
> **No coverage was lost** in 48 → 50. One finding: two negative tests silently stopped
> discriminating (**N-21**), which is an assertion-strength defect, not a coverage gap.
>
> No blocking findings. Everything still open is listed in §16.5 and travels to HG1.

## 16.1 B-6 and the neighbour (item 1a) — closed

**B-6 closed.** §3.1 now strikes the superseded sentence in place — visible, not deleted —
and replaces it with *"`value is None` if and only if `sufficiency_state is
INSUFFICIENT_DATA`; `AVAILABLE` and `LIMITED` both require a value,"* which matches
`src/product_contract/metric_state.py` exactly (E5-1, E5-2).

**The neighbour fix is right, and it is the better of the two catches.** The same entity
bullet opened *"a value (nullable)"* — true under the original AC-15, true under PD-0007's
first ruling, and false under the amendment. It now reads *"a value (nullable only for
`INSUFFICIENT_DATA` — see below)"*, so the field annotation and the invariant sentence
below it now say the same thing. Two lines apart, contradicting each other, is exactly how
B-6 itself survived four rounds; `engineer-02` finding it unprompted is the neighbour-
propagation discipline actually being applied rather than promised.

**Exhaustive grep re-run independently** (E5-3): three hits remain repository-wide, and all
three are correct — struck text in `specs/` (with the strikethrough now properly closed,
N-18), struck text in the plan's §3.1, and a blockquote in PD-0007 quoting the defect it
corrects. No live statement of any superseded AC-15 wording survives anywhere.

`specs/` AC-15 now states the **total** rule, not PD-0007's first ruling, and records that
`engineer-02` flagged it and correctly declined to edit a path outside its write authority.
That is the write-boundary behaving as designed rather than as an obstacle.

## 16.2 The total equivalence (R-15) — verified

**The ruling.** I checked the amendment's own over-tightening question independently: *is
there a legitimate `AVAILABLE`-or-`LIMITED` metric with no value?* I could not find one.
`0.0` is a value and is separately tested; a not-yet-computed metric is not a `MetricResult`
at all, since that type is the envelope a *computed* value travels in; a suppressed-for-
licensing benchmark figure (§11.4) is the only candidate I could construct, and it is not a
§32 sufficiency state, has no reason code, and is not built by this increment. **The
amendment is semantically forced, as it claims.** I also note it closes a finding of my own
that has been open since round 1 — **N-1** (`AVAILABLE` + `value=None` had no rendering in
D3.2) — which no round until now had resolved.

**The implementation.** `__post_init__` implements the biconditional as two clauses (E5-2):
`is_insufficient and value is not None` → raise; `not is_insufficient and value is None` →
raise. Nothing else moved: `_REASON_CODES_REQUIRING_NON_AVAILABLE` is unchanged in
membership, its clause still follows both, and `__init_subclass__` / `__reduce__` are intact.

**The 48 → 50 trace, by target state rather than by count** (E5-4):

| Test | Before | Now | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_available_with_no_value_is_permitted` | positive, `AVAILABLE` + `None` | **inverted** into `test_available_with_no_value_fails` in `AC15NegativeTests` | Correct — it pinned precisely what the amendment forbids. Inverted, not deleted |
| `test_limited_with_no_value_and_no_reason` | positive, `LIMITED` + `None` | renamed `test_limited_with_no_reason_code`, now `LIMITED` + `0.55` | Retargeted; still pins "reason code optional when not `AVAILABLE`" |
| `test_limited_with_no_value_fails` | — | **new**, `LIMITED` + `None` raises | BF-4 itself pinned as a negative |
| `test_dataclasses_replace_permits_a_valid_transition` | `AVAILABLE`→`LIMITED` dropping the value | `AVAILABLE`→`INSUFFICIENT_DATA` dropping the value | Retargeted; the old transition is now invalid |
| `test_dataclasses_replace_to_limited_with_no_value_fails` | — | **new** | Closes the `replace()` route to the BF-4 state |
| `StaleDataNarrowingTests` positives (2) | `value=None` / `value=1.30` | both `value=1.30` | **Retargeted, not deleted.** PD-0006's `STALE_DATA` exemption is still genuinely pinned |
| Tamper/copy/pickle/`__dict__` vectors (5) | `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` + `None` | unchanged | Correctly untouched — still legal to construct, so all round-2/3 seals still tested |
| `TypeValidationTests` (2) | `value=None` + a bad enum | unchanged | Still pass, because the `isinstance` checks precede the value clauses. Order-dependent, but a reorder would fail loudly, not silently |

48 + 2 new = **50**, with one conversion and four retargets, and **nothing deleted**
(E5-5: 50 tests, OK, exit 0, four runs including `PYTHONHASHSEED=31`).

### N-21 (new, non-blocking) — two negative tests silently stopped discriminating

`ReasonCodeCouplingNegativeTests.test_available_with_each_coupled_reason_code_and_no_value_fails`
and `StaleDataNarrowingTests.test_stale_data_is_the_only_exempt_reason_code` both construct
`AVAILABLE` + `value=None` + a coupled reason code, and both assert only
`InvalidMetricResultError`. Under the amendment that construction now trips the
**biconditional** clause before it ever reaches the **reason-code** clause. Neither test can
any longer distinguish which rule fired, and **both would still pass if PD-0006's five-code
coupling were deleted outright.**

Two things follow, and the second corrects the framing in my dispatch:

1. **Coverage is not lost.** `test_available_with_each_coupled_reason_code_and_a_value_fails`
   uses `value=1.30`, so the value clause passes and the coupling clause is what raises.
   That test still discriminates, so the coupling remains genuinely pinned — by **one**
   test where it used to be pinned by three.
2. **`StaleDataNarrowingTests` is not "the only thing pinning the `STALE_DATA` exemption"
   in the way it was described to me.** Its two *positives* pin the exemption and are
   correct (both now carry `value=1.30`). Its *contrast* test no longer pins the contrast,
   and its comment — *"every other reason code fails the same construction that
   `STALE_DATA` above permits"* — is now factually wrong, because the positives use a value
   and the contrast uses `None`, so they are no longer the same construction.

One word in each test (`value=None` → `value=1.30`) restores the discrimination. **Static
analysis from clause order, not executed:** proving it would require mutating
`src/product_contract/metric_state.py` to see the tests still pass, and I may not edit
implementation (NR5-2).

## 16.3 Does the equivalence create or forbid a state the design disagrees with? No — and this is the first clean bijection

I enumerated every constructible state against every §D3.2 row (E5-6):

| Constructible | Rendered by |
|---|---|
| `AVAILABLE` + value, no reason code | row 1 |
| `AVAILABLE` + value + `STALE_DATA` | row 2 |
| `LIMITED` + value, ± any reason code | row 3 (+ row 5 for the five) |
| `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` + `None`, ± any reason code | row 4 (+ row 5 for the five) |

And in the other direction: every row describes a state that can be constructed. Forbidden
by the code — `AVAILABLE`/`LIMITED` + `None`, `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` + value, `AVAILABLE` +
any of the five — and **no row specifies any of them**. Row 5's own text already says the
five attached to `AVAILABLE` is "a defect to reject at construction," which is now exactly
what happens.

**Bijection, both directions, no gap on either side.** BF-1, BF-3 and BF-4 were each an
instance of one side permitting or specifying something the other could not match; this is
the first pass where that class has no remaining instance. It is also why the amendment was
the right shape: it closed the class, not the instance.

**One observation, explicitly not a finding and not my remit.** §D3.2 row 1's rationale
column still reads *"this is the only state permitted to render a number at all"* — a
leftover from before rows 2 and 3 existed, and contradicted by those rows in the same table.
The *rendering* column is correct and the contract matches it; only the parenthetical
rationale is stale. `designs/` is `designer-04`'s and `design_review` is running
concurrently, so I am flagging it for whoever owns that file rather than reviewing it.

**One disposition change on an out-of-scope item, reported because the item is travelling.**
R-15 changes the shape of **N-17/NF-5**: `LIMITED` + `CALCULATION_ERROR` now *requires* a
value, so the pairing that used to be available and sane — a calculation-errored metric
carrying no number — is now illegal, and the only legal form of that pairing presents a
number. I am not reopening it; it should reach `quant_analyst` and HG1 in this form rather
than in its round-4 form.
